Second, they comply with international standards like ISO/IEC to ensure consistent and robust data protection practices. Third, they implement software development practices, including open-source vulnerability scanning, to identify and fix security weaknesses in the codebase. Fourth, they use data anonymization techniques with pseudonyms to protect patient identities and reduce the risk of data exposure. Finally, they establish a comprehensive incident response plan as part of their audit and monitoring processes, enabling rapid detection and mitigation of security threats.
